key_insight: The paper introduces probabilistic approximate quantum error correction (PAQEC) to tailor recovery for generalized amplitude-damping noise, achieving quadratic fidelity loss with a five-qubit permutation-invariant code.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more resource-efficient route to high-fidelity quantum memory and error correction for realistic near-term quantum hardware affected by damping-type noise.
method: Combine approximate QEC with post-selected probabilistic recovery.
Design a five-qubit permutation-invariant code specialized for generalized amplitude-damping noise.
Optimize the recovery map using Charnes-Cooper reformulation and semidefinite programming.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the proposed code under probabilistic recovery reduces fidelity loss to quadratic order in the damping strength, outperforming conventional deterministic QEC for this noise model.
watch_item: Probabilistic recovery relies on post-selection, so practical gains may depend on acceptance probability, hardware overhead, and how often successful recoveries occur.
paper_title: Quantum Codes for Generalized Amplitude-damping Noise
